touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Lives in cairn/tools/. Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/

The line between tool and machine is simple vs. complex, and it is measured, not judged. A tool calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Anything that calls another component, or owns state it must gate, is a machine. A tool that uses other tools is a machine. Tools and machines are peers in the tree; the rung is complexity, not rank. (Q#1, Akien 2026-11-03: "strict")
A device holds machines and uses tools (from cairn/tools/). A tool's data for that device lives under the device: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/
A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.
build_inspector: python sieves run after a build; reds a component that fails one (no charter, no proofs, a silent device, ...). "We find a new thing, we add a new sieve." → CodeMother (10.3.5)
A tool, not a machine, even though it spans several files.
system_word: case-folding for system words (device names, verbs, statuses), so anything you type is case-insensitive.
